title: When Forgetting Becomes a Disease
notes: Start in silence with one small connection. Right once: expand into a brain-inspired network. Right again: move the same network to the right and reveal the title. Right again advances to the memory activity. The illustration is conceptual and does not model an individual brain.

title: Five words. Ten seconds.
notes: Press Start or Right to show the five words. After ten seconds the words disappear, or advance manually to hide them earlier. Ask for responses, then Right to reveal the answer. A brief classroom memory task cannot diagnose dementia. Distraction and attention also affect performance.

title: When does forgetting change everyday life?
notes: Introduce the question of everyday independence, then advance directly into the four connected themes.

title: Four themes, one connected journey
notes: The four central themes rise from the previous roadmap. Its same particles gather into a white S-shaped path; a blue stripe traces the order.

title: Dementia in China
src: Jia et al. (2020), The Lancet Public Health. doi:10.1016/S2468-2667(20)30185-7
notes: Explain that 6.0% is the age- and sex-adjusted dementia prevalence among Chinese adults aged 60 or older in this national study, not the prevalence in the entire population or a current live count. The 100-dot illustration shows the rounded 6-in-100 proportion.

title: Zhang San
notes: Invite an audience vote. Select an answer or press Right to reveal the teaching interpretation. Occasional forgetting with preserved independent daily function fits normal aging in this simplified example. This classroom example is not a clinical diagnosis.

title: Li Si
notes: Invite an audience vote. Select an answer or press Right to reveal the teaching interpretation. Greater cognitive difficulty than expected for age, with independence largely preserved, suggests possible mild cognitive impairment. MCI does not always progress to dementia. This classroom example is not a clinical diagnosis.

title: Ma Dongmei
notes: Invite an audience vote. Select an answer or press Right to reveal the teaching interpretation. This example involves cognitive changes interfering with independent daily functioning. It needs professional assessment. These are illustrative cases, not diagnoses. This classroom example is not a clinical diagnosis.

title: The cognitive continuum
src: National Institute on Aging (2022); WHO, Dementia
notes: First compare the three conditions. Then reveal the key distinction. This is a comparison, not a guaranteed sequence of progression. MCI does not inevitably progress to dementia.

title: Dementia is an umbrella term
src: WHO, Dementia; Alzheimer’s Association, What is dementia?
notes: The same word Dementia carries over from the continuum. Distinguish dementia as a syndrome from Alzheimer’s disease as one cause. Do not imply that every person with dementia has Alzheimer’s disease.

title: What happens in dementia?
notes: Advance through cell damage, disrupted communication, and effects on daily life. The neural network gradually loses pathways and some nodes dim. It is a simplified conceptual illustration, not a claim that all dementias share one mechanism.

title: Assessment can change the explanation
src: National Institute on Aging; Alzheimer’s Association; supplied teaching deck
notes: Reveal the three examples individually. Professional assessment can identify treatable causes of similar symptoms. This does not mean that all dementia is reversible.

title: Risk has more than one source
src: WHO, Dementia; Livingston et al. (2024); Shi et al. (2023)
notes: Distinguish risk factors from causes and explain that risk is not destiny. The next two slides focus on environmental evidence. The US cohort used Medicare records from 2000–2017 and two independently derived exposure datasets. These observational associations do not directly estimate an individual’s risk in China.

title: PM₂.₅ constituents and dementia
notes: Bars animate from the same baseline and use exact exposure-I point estimates reported in the article. Hover, focus or click a bar. Switch the outcome to compare. Right reveals the causal limitation before advancing. No raw exposure-II or CI values are invented. The full original figure is available by clicking the source control.

title: Concentration–response curves
notes: Select a constituent and disease outcome. Preserve the original figure without inventing raw spline data. The source figure excludes the outer 1% of concentrations. Do not read a high-concentration downturn as proof of a protective effect. The slider only reveals the original panel.

title: Risk reduction
src: Livingston et al. (2024), The Lancet Commission. doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(24)01296-0
notes: The background shifts to light as the focus changes from disruption to action. First show 45%, then move that same statistic into the 100-dot visual. This is the Commission’s theoretical population potential across 14 modifiable risk factors, not a guaranteed individual risk reduction and not evidence of curing established dementia.

title: Everyday risk reduction
src: WHO, Dementia; WHO physical activity guidelines; supplied teaching deck
notes: Right advances through five actions. The visual creates supportive outer connections without restoring the damaged internal neural pattern. The physical-activity figure is general WHO guidance, not a dementia-specific guaranteed dose. Follow individual medical advice when appropriate.

title: Playing mahjong and brain health
src: Tian et al. (2022), Frontiers in Aging Neuroscience. doi:10.3389/fnagi.2022.966647
notes: The cohort study compared card or mahjong frequency. It found an association, not a causal effect. The activity requires memory and decisions and involves social contact, but the study did not prove these mechanisms. People who play often may differ in other ways.

title: Shanghai: support for caregivers
src: Changning District Government (2024); Shanghai Civil Affairs Bureau (2025). Photo and local source attribution from the supplied deck.
notes: Retain the real workshop photo from the original deck. Advance through connection, training, home guidance and respite. Local citations are inherited from the supplied deck and have not been independently verified in full. Present them as examples of caregiver support, not proven dementia-prevention programmes.

title: Daily life at Juradorf
src: SRO (2022); nefl / SDA (2022); dahlia oberaargau official gallery. Sources and photos from the supplied deck.
notes: The same image frame moves subtly as Walk, Cook and Find reveal different official photos from the original deck. These are care design ideas, not claims that the built environment cures dementia. Retain the transferable ideas for community care centres in China.

title: Support changes everyday life
notes: The surviving neural pattern stays fragmented. A wider ring of support forms around it. The change represents supportive relationships and environments rather than restored brain tissue or a cure.

title: Memory matters. So does independence.
notes: Return to the opening composition. The neural pattern remains partly disrupted, surrounded by support. A forgotten classroom word differs from persistent cognitive decline affecting daily life. Ask for one takeaway and invite questions.
